rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Round End 4 Game End Overview Gain Spicy through tricks across Three Rounds, but gaining a prescribed number of Spicy or no Spicy will score you bonus points Turn The lead player can play any card from their hand The follow players must play the same suit if possible, otherwise can play any card The player who played the highest value card in the lead suit wins the trick and also claims the visible Spicy card as a reward before starting the next trick Fibonacho cards can be used as Trumps, which beat the Lead suit, but only if TWO Fibonachos are played in a round In case two Fibonacho cards are tied for the highest, the last one played will take the trick. Round End The round ends when everyone is out of cards At which point, sum up all the Spicy you've won Normally, the quantity of Spicy is your score If you meet a number of Spicy equal to a quantity shown on the Spicy table, score that value instead e.g. 5 Spicy scores 8 points If you have 0 Spicy, your score is that of the highest scorer Game End At the end of Round 3, add up your score for each round, the player with the most points wins!

[Rating: 5/10] Cool to see some unique designs in the crowded trick taking genre. While I love to see new innovations, this one wasn't for me, personally. The way trump activated made for a few interesting decisions, but also made some bad hands feel even worse to play as you were forced to just enable another player to win. Multiple times my decision came down to picking who got to take a trick, but not me, which felt a little off.

[Rating: 5/10] Trick-taker with three suits. You must follow suit if you can, the twist being that the second Fibonacci number played to a trick turns all the Fibonacci cards into trumps. Meaning hand management, short-suiting and counting cards becomes pretty meaningless because there’s no way to know if this will be a trumped trick or not. The number of points for winning a trick (0-5) is revealed at the start of the trick, adding to the randomness. There’s a big reward for going misere but it’s easy to be forced to win a trick you weren’t expecting, leading you to be thankful it only goes 3 rounds.
